answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash it when that identity is caught duplicating another agent’s signed work or coordinating a rule-breaking vote. A reputation trellis links identities to prior interactions, so a newcomer’s claims count less until independent peers validate them. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can buy identities, but must lock up capital in every one and risks losing the bonds. Timber and opal can serve as accepted bond assets, making the attack costly rather than free.
